title: One Sauna Session Sends White Blood Cells Surging
paragraphs: Researchers at the University of Eastern Finland studied what a sauna does to the body. Fifty-one adults took part, and their average age was 50. Each person stayed in a hot sauna for 30 minutes and took a short cold shower in the middle.

The scientists measured the blood before and after the sauna. They found more white blood cells in the blood after the session. These cells help the body fight germs. The numbers went back to normal within 30 minutes.
This does not mean saunas make people healthier. The study looked at only one sauna session. It did not look at long-term health.

questions.q: What happened to the white blood cells?
questions.a: The number in the blood went up for a short time.

questions.q: Why can we not say saunas make people healthier?
questions.a: The study looked at only one sauna session.
